s:
With reference to physical capital in Indian economy, consider the following pairs: Items Category
1. Farmer's plough Working capital
2. Computer Fixed Capital
3. Yarn used by the weaver Fixed Capital
4. Petrol Working capital
How many of the above pairs are correctly matched ?
x: Fixed capital refers to long-term tangible assets used in the production of goods and services. Tools, machines, buildings etc. can be used in production over many years, and are called fixed capital. These tools and machines range from very simple tools such as a farmer’s plough to sophisticated machines such as generators, turbines, computers, etc. Hence, pair 1 is incorrect while pair 2 is correctly matched. Production of goods and services requires a variety of raw materials such as the yarn used by the weaver, the clay used by the potter and fuels like petrol and diesel used in machines and transportation. Also, some money is always required during production to make payments and buy other necessary items. Raw materials and money in hand are called working capital. Hence, pair 3 is incorrect while pair 4 is correctly matched.

x: The NSO follows the IMF's Special Data Dissemination Standard (SDDS).

s: Indicate the vital change in the measurement of National Income of India recently :
o: Both the base year and calculation method have
Base year has been changed from 2004-05 to 2011-12

x: The CSO, in 2015, replaced the GDP series with the base year 2004-05 with a new series that used 2011-12 as a baseline for national accounts. In the new series, the CSO did away with Gross Domestic Product (GDP) at factor cost and adopted the international practice of valuing industry-wise estimates as Gross Value Added (GVA) at basic prices. The new series has followed the guidelines of the United Nations' System of National Accounts (UNSNA) 2008, replacing the earlier template of UNSNA 1994. Thus, option (a) is the correct answer. The new GDP series with the base year 2022-23 was released by the MoSPI on 27 February, 2026.

s: What was the headline measure of value added under the 2011-12 national accounts series?

It showed unusually high manufacturing growth that did not match physical indicators
It used only household survey data for manufacturing
It completely excluded the private corporate sector
x: The series was criticised for unusually high manufacturing growth that was inconsistent with physical indicators and for overestimating the private corporate sector.

s: According to former Chief Economic Adviser Arvind Subramanian, what was India's GDP growth during 2011-17 under the 2011-12 series?

s: The 2011-12 base year series of India's national accounts, released in 2015, replaced which earlier base year?
